returnRoutes.title: Return routes
returnRoutes.hint: Measure this server’s default route to three carrier targets. Independent of proxy/WireGuard business paths. ASN lookups disclose public hop IPs to Team Cymru through DNS.
returnRoutes.requirement: Requires bosun ≥ 0.69.0 and a compatible probe tool with ICMP permissions. IPv4 and IPv6 are tested separately.
returnRoutes.scheduleHint: Save schedules for the selected region and family. First check runs after one interval.
returnRoutes.changed: Observed networks changed: {{before}} → {{after}}. Missing replies or ASN data can also cause this; this is not a confirmed downgrade.
returnRoutes.install: Use the tool check and install buttons above; verify ICMP permissions in the server or container.
returnRoutes.limits: Labels identify observed transit networks, not guaranteed service tiers or quality. GIA is only a hypothesis; a missing hop is not proof of packet loss. Targets may become unavailable. Results are visible only to administrators.

tools.title: Probe tool
tools.working: Waiting for the server to check the tool, or download, verify and test NextTrace…
tools.hint: Installs a pinned, checksum-verified NextTrace Tiny into the server data directory. System traceroute remains a fallback. No system packages or container privileges are changed.
tools.permission: ICMP raw sockets are unavailable. Check NET_RAW/container permissions; installing a tool cannot grant these permissions.

nodeAddresses.createHint: Public IPs are optional by default. After pairing, bosun fills and follows addresses after repeated confirmation; IPv6 stays empty when unavailable. Requires bosun with address detection.
nodeAddresses.fixedHint: Fixed public entries do not follow detected changes. For NAT / private lines, enter the provider entry and configure port mappings separately.
nodeAddresses.internalHint: Optional. Enter the server’s existing internal IP. Used to identify relay sources and by forwards that explicitly select the server internal address. Filling it in does not create a private network or change existing paths.
nodeAddresses.title: Machine public addresses and entry
nodeAddresses.hint: bosun probes public IPv4 / IPv6 every 30 seconds for the first 3 minutes after startup, then every 5 minutes. These are outbound public addresses; NAT egress may differ from the client entry address.
nodeAddresses.waiting: Waiting for a fresh address report from an updated bosun. Old values are for reference only.
nodeAddresses.behavior: Existing entries stay fixed by default. Following requires two consecutive confirmed probes before updating this address and eligible automatic DNS. Failed probes retain old values. Manually editing a server address disables following for that family. Explicit NAT/line entries, subscription addresses and WG endpoints stay unchanged.
nodeAddresses.dnsPending: Address updated; DNS sync is pending or retrying. See DNS health and change history.
nodeAddresses.confirming: Address detected; waiting for another independent sample to confirm it.
nodeAddresses.applying: Address confirmed; waiting to update the entry address and synchronize DNS.

dashboard.title: Overview
dashboard.workspaceHint: Review server issues and daily tasks, then follow business activity.
dashboard.stale: The values below are from the last successful refresh.
dashboard.operationsHint: Offline means no contact for three minutes. Self-check results are the last report; acknowledged incidents remain unresolved until recovery.
dashboard.utcHint: Daily totals use UTC. Today is still in progress; traffic is recorded usage, not network availability.

nodes.title: Servers
nodes.subtitle: One machine, one bosun. The panel pushes inbounds and users; bosun runs the cores and reports traffic.
nodes.name: Name
nodes.pairHint: Run either command as root on the server: it installs bosun and pairs it. The code is valid for 24h, single use.
nodes.repairHint: Revokes the current token and issues a new code; the server must pair again.
nodes.upgradeConfirm: {{name}} downloads bosun {{version}} and restarts into it; cores restart, users drop for a few seconds. Continue?
nodes.upgradeQueued: Upgrade queued; the server applies it on its next report
nodes.upgradeAllConfirm: {{count}} servers will move to bosun {{version}}, each on its next report. Continue?
nodes.certProblem: A certificate failed or expires soon
nodes.manualHint: bosun already installed? Adopt with the code, or copy the config snippet:
nodes.monitorUrlHint: If you run another probe , paste this server's page there; the server page shows a link.
nodes.domainHint: This server's host name, e.g. jp1.example.com. New inbounds and subscription nodes default to it; certificates are matched and pushed by name.
nodes.domainInvalid: Enter one fully qualified host name without a scheme, port, path or wildcard.
nodes.domainSharedHint: For DNS round robin, CDN or load balancing. Captain stops changing DNS for this name and keeps existing records. Manage DNS and compatible protocols, ports and credentials on the servers yourself.
nodes.domainSharedConflictHint: Automatic DNS updates for this name will stop across all servers and ingresses to prevent overwrites.
nodes.domainLegacyHint: Multiple servers use this domain, so automatic DNS updates are paused. Other fields remain editable. Choose a unique domain, or explicitly enable sharing and manage DNS externally.
nodes.domainConflictHint: Choose another domain, or enable sharing if this is intentional and manage DNS externally.
nodes.domainCheckUnavailable: Domain preview is unavailable. The server will validate again when saving.
nodes.domainDNSSkipped: Saved, but automatic DNS updates were skipped for a shared domain or address conflict. Existing records were not changed.
nodes.advIngressHint: NAT / dedicated-line addresses and port ranges
nodes.advRoutingHint: Default proxy outbound and routing rules for this server
nodes.advForwardsHint: Forward ports to another server (front relay)
nodes.doctorFailHint: The server's last self-check had failures; open the server page
nodes.decoyHint: The server serves a real HTTPS site for its domain on loopback and REALITY inbounds use it as the handshake target: probes see a genuine certificate for your name and fallback traffic never leaves the box. Needs the domain above.
nodes.decoyUpstreamHint: Blank serves the built-in placeholder; an http(s) URL is reverse-proxied
nodes.speedLimitHint: 0 = none. Applies to users on this server without a plan limit; a plan limit wins. Needs Linux with nft and tc; only xray / sing-box protocols are shaped.
nodes.advOverridesHint: Core options the panel does not model
nodes.mitaQuotasHint: Also write users' allowances into mita's own quotas so the core blocks overuse while the panel is unreachable. The window is the plan's reset cycle (monthly = rolling 31 days), so right after a calendar reset mita may still block for a few days.
nodes.rollbackConfirm: Put the previous bosun build back on {{name}} (now {{version}}). Cores restart, users drop for a few seconds. Continue?
nodes.rollbackQueued: Rollback queued; the server restarts on its previous build
nodes.doctorNotApplied: Inbounds not applied on the server
nodes.egressByIngressHint: Multi-IP host: an inbound bound to a specific address sends its traffic out from that address (sing-box, xray, hysteria). Set each inbound's bind address; any-address inbounds keep the default route; ignored when a default landing outbound is set. Needs bosun ≥ 0.44.
nodes.proxySettingsHint: Configure this server’s address mappings, proxy routing and core options.
nodes.proxySettingsMoved: These settings are now in server details. Select a server to continue.
nodes.hostTrafficHint: Server traffic counts selected interfaces over the reset cycle, with upload and download shown separately. It includes proxy, forwarding and system traffic; it is not user-plan billing or the provider’s invoice. The cycle ends at the next reset boundary.
nodes.proxyTrafficHint: UTC-day customer proxy traffic is attributed to the exit server. Reverse WireGuard / VLESS Reverse is measured on the front server and attributed to its exit without charging twice. Raw forwarding and system traffic are excluded.
nodes.proxyTrafficPartial: Attribution is fully recorded from {{date}} UTC; earlier history may be incomplete.

inbounds.title: Inbounds
inbounds.subtitle: Protocol servers on the server. Bind a group to restrict who may use it.
inbounds.settingsHint: JSON matching bosun spec.Inbound. Automatic TLS: "tls":{"mode":1,"server_name":"domain","auto_cert":true,"acme":"http"} (acme: http or dns)
inbounds.recipeHint: Pick a recipe to fill the fields; edit anything afterwards.

recipes.vlessRealityDesc: Best TCP stealth; needs an x25519 key pair.
recipes.hysteria2Desc: QUIC, best throughput on lossy lines; needs a certificate.
recipes.mieruDesc: Low-signature TCP for IPLC and carrier QoS.
recipes.ss2022Desc: Lightweight; needs a base64 server key.
recipes.snellDesc: Surge's protocol with a shared PSK; only Surge / mihomo / Stash can use it.
recipes.wireguardDesc: Whole-device VPN over UDP; for lines and internal networks.
recipes.socks5Desc: Plain text with username/password; for lines, LANs or local programs.
recipes.shadowtlsDesc: Looks like a real HTTPS site to anything that probes the port; sing-box only.

inbounds.mieruStrategyHint: Same presets as nobrand-oneclick: dedicated line = no obfuscation, public = conservative, stealth adds fragmentation and padding; custom edits traffic_pattern below directly.
inbounds.ingressDirectHint: Clients dial the server's public address or domain.
inbounds.ingressHint: Clients connect to {{host}}; local ports / mappings: {{ports}}.
inbounds.ingressNewHint: Saving creates the ingress first, then the inbound.
inbounds.ingressNewFields: Copy these from the provider's network information page:
inbounds.lineOnlyHint: This server has no public address or domain and is reached only through a line ingress: pick one, or the subscription has no usable address.
inbounds.mieruBothHint: BOTH = TCP on this port, UDP on port +1
inbounds.snellHint: Without multi-user, Snell has one shared PSK for everyone (snell-server): no per-user accounting or limits. Surge, Stash and mihomo support Snell; sing-box and URI subscriptions leave it out.
inbounds.realityScanHint: Server-side TLS 1.3, h2, X25519, certificate, wire-record size and CDN screening. This does not verify a complete REALITY connection.
inbounds.realityRecordHint: Observed record limit: {{limit}} B. Basic screening only; a complete REALITY connection is still required.
inbounds.realityRecordUnknownHint: The server did not report a completed record check. Older bosun versions do not measure it.
inbounds.realityRecordTooLarge: Observed TLS record is too large: {{bytes}} B > {{limit}} B. Choose another target.
inbounds.realityCdnHint: CDN-hosted sites get found by "preferred IP" scanners, whose users then relay traffic through your server
inbounds.fallbackLimitHint: Connections that fail REALITY auth are relayed to the target; throttled, a discovered server is worthless to scanners. Xray only.
inbounds.realityTargetHint: Current target: {{host}}. It must speak TLS 1.3 + h2 and not sit on Cloudflare or another CDN.
inbounds.realityNeedsNode: Save the server first to probe from it.
inbounds.ingressBindHint: Leave the listen address blank to bind the line IP {{ip}}.
inbounds.useDecoyHint: SNI becomes the decoy domain, handshake target 127.0.0.1:4443
inbounds.wgHint: Standard WireGuard for routers and system VPNs. For multiple devices, create a separate WireGuard device subscription for each device in the user portal or user details. Sharing one identity can cause connections to switch between devices. Regular subscriptions remain compatible.
inbounds.wgAddressHint: Client addresses are assigned from this network by user id
inbounds.noSniffHint: On by default: reads the real host from TLS/HTTP so domain rules apply. Turn off only if sniffing breaks a client.
inbounds.acceptProxyHint: Only for an inbound reached exclusively through this panel's forwards: the relay sends the client's address in a PROXY protocol header, so online devices and logs show the real client. Direct connections to such an inbound fail. xray only.
inbounds.snellMultiUserHint: Served by sing-box: every user connects with their own key and traffic is counted per user; the PSK stays the server key. Only sing-box clients (1.14+) can present a user key, so this line appears in sing-box subscriptions only. Obfs tls is not available.
inbounds.shadowTLSHint: The public port performs a real TLS handshake with the site below and only lets authenticated clients through to this inbound, which moves to loopback. sing-box serves it; every user gets their own ShadowTLS password on top of the Shadowsocks key. Clients: mihomo, Stash, sing-box, Surge, Loon, Shadowrocket.
inbounds.shadowTLSHandshakeHint: A real HTTPS site with TLS 1.3, unrelated to this server; its certificate is what a prober sees
inbounds.shadowTLSStrictHint: Refuse a ClientHello the site itself would not accept

coreSelection.preview: Expected core: {{core}}. Automatic follows the server’s priority; REALITY prefers Xray.
coreSelection.enabledHint: Only compatible cores are listed. Enable unavailable cores in the server configuration first.
coreSelection.unknown: Core availability is unknown (older, offline or unreported server). The server will validate on apply.
coreSelection.unavailable: This core is not enabled on the server. Enable it there or choose another core.
coreSelection.noAvailable: No enabled core supports this configuration. Enable a compatible core on the server first.
coreSelection.loadFailed: Could not check cores. Retrying automatically; check the connection.
coreSelection.invalidJSON: Fix the settings JSON to check compatible cores.

reasons.protocol: This core does not support the protocol. Choose another core.
reasons.transport: This core does not support the transport. Choose another core.
reasons.unknown: This core is not recognized. Choose a compatible core.
reasons.reverse: This protocol or core does not support managed VLESS Reverse with per-user accounting.
reasons.privateAccess: Private access requires a recent capability report from a supported server and core.
reasons.listenAddress: This Mieru build cannot bind a specific listening IP. Use mita.
reasons.wireguardReverse: Reverse WireGuard requires a fresh capability report from a supported Linux server and Xray core.
reasons.privateAccessCoreOnly: Core-only needs a supported sing-box server, disabled egress guard and a fresh capability report; Xray and managed reverse tunnels are unsupported.
reasons.privateAccessPolicyUnknown: Automatic policy requires a fresh server report with separate policy capabilities.
reasons.privateAccessRuntime: The runtime prerequisites are not satisfied. Check the server readiness details.
reasons.privateAccessConfirmation: Confirm authorization under core-only protection before saving.

entryCategories.label: Node category
entryCategories.hint: For display only; does not change access, billing, tags or subscription order.
entryCategories.managerHint: Give each subscription node one display category. Category order is separate from node order. Categories do not change permissions or billing.
entryCategories.empty: No categories yet. Existing nodes remain unclassified.
entryCategories.name: Category name
entryCategories.deleteHint: Delete “{{name}}”? Its nodes will remain and become unclassified.
entryCategories.batchLimit: Select no more than 10,000 nodes at a time.

entries.title: Subscription nodes
entries.name: Name
entries.dragHint: Drag the handle to reorder nodes in subscriptions
entries.clientExtraHint: JSON object merged into this node’s proxy in mihomo/Stash/sing-box subscriptions, e.g. tfo, smux, dialer-proxy, ip-version.

users.title: Users
users.subtitle: Accounts, subscriptions and balances.
users.grantHint: By default the plan starts now next to what the user has (the same plan renews); it can also wait until the current plans lapse, or replace them all.
users.topUpHint: Positive credits, negative debits, in cents.
users.rotateHint: Old permanent subscription links stop working immediately. Temporary links and proxy credentials downloaded from regular subscriptions remain valid. All WireGuard device links are revoked immediately; downloaded device configurations stop working after the servers sync.
users.deleteBlocked: This user has orders, commission records or invited users and cannot be deleted. To disable the account while preserving its history, set its status to Banned.
users.idHint: Leave blank to assign automatically. Choosing a large ID does not advance automatic numbering.

plans.title: Plans
plans.subtitle: Price, period, quota and group.
plans.name: Name
plans.pricesHint: One per line: days:cents, e.g. 90:2700 for a quarter at ¥27. The price above is the default period.

settings.acmeHint: Servers whose inbounds have “auto_cert” use this account with Let's Encrypt. HTTP needs port 80 reachable on the server; DNS goes through Cloudflare. Pushed to every server on save.
settings.cfTokenHint: DNS challenge only; permission Zone.DNS edit. Blank keeps, - clears
settings.cfTokenSet: Set; blank keeps it, - clears it
settings.subUrlsHint: Addresses used in user subscription links, one per line, picked at random; blank means the site URL. [1-9] and [uuid] placeholders work with wildcard DNS. These hosts serve only the subscription path; everything else is 404.
settings.oidcHint: One entry per provider: Casdoor, Authentik, Keycloak, Google or any standard OIDC issuer. issuer is the discovery root, e.g. https://door.example.com; leave client_secret blank to keep it.
settings.passwordLogin: Allow password login (off = external login only)
settings.oidcCallback: Redirect URI to register at the provider:
settings.noticeHint: Shown at the top of the portal home page when enabled.
settings.inviteHint: Users share /?ref=CODE; when an invitee pays, a share of the amount is credited to the inviter's balance.
settings.surplusHint: When a user switches to another plan, the unused part of the current one (by remaining time, or remaining traffic for plans without expiry) is credited against the new order.
settings.shortLinksHint: Subscription URLs become /s/<code> instead of /sub/<long token>; old links keep working.
settings.autoFlagsHint: Prefix node names that have no flag emoji with their region flag (set or detected from the name), e.g. 🇯🇵 Tokyo.
settings.singlePlanHint: On: buying a different plan replaces the current one (surplus credit applies). Off: plans stack, servers are combined and traffic is counted per plan.
settings.hwidHint: Count devices by the x-hwid header instead of online IP for clients that send it (the standard shared with Remnawave and Happ). The plan device limit then applies per device; clients without the header still count by IP.
settings.hwidRequireHint: Clients that send no x-hwid get 404. Only turn on when all your users use HWID-capable clients.
settings.hwidFallbackHint: When neither the user nor a plan sets a device limit. 0 = unlimited.
settings.hwidAnnounceHint: Shown by Happ when a device is over the limit.
settings.infoLinesHint: One dummy server per line at the top of every subscription, named with the account state. Also usable in subscription node names. Variables: {{DAYS_LEFT}}, {{EXPIRE_DATE}}, {{TRAFFIC_LEFT}}, {{TRAFFIC_USED}}, {{TRAFFIC_LIMIT}}, {{USED_PERCENT}}, {{STATUS}}, {{STATUS:ACTIVE=✅|EXPIRED=😓|LIMITED=⛔|DISABLED=❌}}, {{PLAN}}, {{EMAIL}}, {{USERNAME}}

update.title: Version and updates
update.devBuild: Development build: online updates are not offered.
update.containerHint: Enable the host updater once using the installer command below. It replaces the image and preserves deployment settings.
update.applyConfirm: Download {{version}}, verify it, replace the running binary and restart. The console is down for a few seconds; servers are unaffected. Continue?
update.rollbackConfirm: Switch back to {{version}} and restart. Continue?
update.restartConfirm: The process exits and systemd or Docker starts it again. Continue?
update.restartingHint: Waiting for the service to come back. The page reloads by itself and you stay signed in.
update.restartTimeout: No response within 30 minutes. Check the service and upgrade status before retrying.
update.hostFailed: Upgrade failed. Inspect the host updater status and backup before retrying; do not downgrade an already migrated database.
update.preparing: Submitting the upgrade request and preparing the update…

site.title: Brand and homepage
site.subtitle: Website branding, the public homepage and shared appearance settings. Changes take effect after saving.
site.globeHint: Markers and illustrative connections use the selected locations; they do not represent live traffic or node health.
site.locations: Manual locations (JSON array: name, lat, lng)
site.featuresHint: icon: bolt, shield, world, devices, refresh, headset
site.overrideHint: For a fully custom page drop your own index.html into the site/ folder of the data directory; Captain serves it as is.
site.themeHint: Shared branding: primary colour, radius and font. The colour-scheme setting below applies to the portal; the admin console is unaffected.
site.publicAppearanceHint: The homepage and public service-status page start in light mode. Visitors can switch light/dark with the header icon; this browser remembers the choice, without account synchronization.
site.injectHint: Inserted verbatim into every portal and landing page: analytics, chat widgets. Admin-only; only paste code you trust.
site.homepageHint: After disabling and saving, visitors who are not signed in open the login page; signed-in users enter the user center.
site.homepageRetained: Homepage content is retained. You can expand and edit it while the homepage is disabled.
site.homepageMapHint: This map selection applies only to the homepage. Manual locations and the hub are shared with the service-status map and can be edited in Advanced settings.
site.sharedLinksHint: These links are used by public pages and the user center. Disabling the homepage does not disable them.
site.sharedMapHint: Manual locations and the hub are shared by the homepage and service-status map when the manual source is selected. Disabling the homepage does not change the status page.

mail.title: Mail
mail.hint: Powers registration codes, password reset and expiry/traffic reminders. SMTP works everywhere; use the Resend API when the host blocks mail ports. Send a test after saving.
mail.reminders: Remind 3 days before expiry and at the traffic thresholds
mail.thresholdsHint: One notice per threshold per quota period, e.g. 60, 80, 90.
mail.languageHint: What users receive; the console language is per staff account

registration.title: Registration limits
registration.hint: The master switch controls password and external signup. Email and invitation limits apply to both; IP limits and CAPTCHA apply to password signup.
registration.suffixesHint: One domain per line; blank = any
registration.enabledHint: Saving takes effect immediately. Off blocks password sign-up and automatic account creation through external login. Existing users can still sign in, and administrators can still create accounts.
registration.inherited: No master override has been saved. Current access follows the deployment and external login settings.

tickets.title: Tickets
tickets.subtitle: Questions from users. Replies reach them by Telegram or email.
tickets.subject: Subject

gifts.title: Gift codes
gifts.subtitle: Generate single-use codes in batches: balance top-up, plan, extra traffic or extra days.
gifts.generated: {{count}} codes generated (shown once, copy them now)
gifts.deleteHint: Only unused codes are removed; redeemed ones stay for the record.

articles.title: Knowledge base
articles.subtitle: Guides shown under Help in the portal, written in Markdown and grouped by category.

clients.title: Client management
clients.hint: Check official stable releases, cache selected installers, then save the versions and visibility you want to offer. Checking or downloading does not publish changes.
clients.name: Name

telegram.title: Telegram bot
telegram.hint: Create a bot with @BotFather and paste its token. Linked users can query their subscription and traffic and get expiry, traffic and ticket notices; new orders and tickets go to the admin chat.
telegram.adminChatHint: Message the bot once, then read your numeric ID from @userinfobot or getUpdates

trial.title: Trial plan
trial.hint: Every new account gets this plan once, whether it signed up with a password or an external login.

withdrawals.title: Withdrawals
withdrawals.subtitle: Commission payout requests. Pay outside Captain and mark paid; rejecting returns the amount to the user's commission balance.

admins.title: Staff
admins.subtitle: Console accounts and roles. The last admin cannot be demoted, disabled or deleted.
admins.matrixText:
Admin: everything.
Operator: everything except settings, system, staff accounts and the landing page.
Support: tickets, plus read-only users, orders, plans and the dashboard.

webhooks.title: Event webhooks
webhooks.hint: Registration, payments, tickets, withdrawals and expiries are POSTed as JSON to your URLs, for n8n, scripts or a CRM. X-Captain-Event names the event; X-Captain-Signature is an HMAC-SHA256 of the body under the secret.

subTemplates.subtitle: The document skeleton for each client format. Captain fills in the servers; rules, groups and General settings are yours to edit.
subTemplates.hintYaml: YAML template: the proxies key is replaced with the servers; the placeholder inside any proxy-group list expands to every server name. Placeholders:
subTemplates.hintIni: Text template: the placeholders become the server lines and the comma-joined names. Placeholders:
subTemplates.hintNodeList: Loon and Quantumult X remote subscriptions are node lists, so the default is just the lines; a full config here must be imported as a configuration in the client.

probe.hint: Off by default. When on, servers send host metrics every few seconds; the panel aggregates minute/hour/day series and serves a status page. Using another probe? Leave it off and servers send nothing extra.
probe.pathHint: Blank = not served on the main domain, e.g. /status
probe.hostsHint: You can use a subdomain of your existing domain, such as probe.example.com; separate multiple domains with commas. Point each domain to your current Captain instance and configure HTTPS. If you use a reverse proxy, add the domain there too. Saving here does not perform these steps automatically.
probe.tasksHint: Servers probe these targets on a schedule and report latency; carrier latency is built in.
probe.carriersHint: One per line: name address:port. Empty uses the NextTrace Beijing defaults for this IP version; a custom list replaces all three.
probe.pageEnabledHint: Turning off the page keeps data collection and alerts running.
probe.financeCurrencyHint: Convert homepage cost totals using reference exchange rates. Server prices and detail pages keep their original currencies.
probe.carrierModesHint: Each protocol and IP version keeps its own targets. Empty lists use NextTrace Beijing Telecom, Unicom and Mobile. TCP port 80 may not respond; ICMP requires permission on the server.
probe.carriersICMPHint: One per line: name hostname or IP (no port). Empty uses the NextTrace Beijing defaults for this IP version; a custom list replaces all three.

nodeProbe.limitInvalid: Enter a non-negative limit of at least 1 byte, or 0 for unlimited (less than 8192 TB).
nodeProbe.modeHint: Server network interfaces: outbound means sent (TX); inbound means received (RX).

external.title: External nodes
external.subtitle: Import other providers' share links or airport subscriptions and offer them in your subscriptions. No bosun behind them, so traffic is not charged to user quotas.
external.name: Name
external.subUrlHint: Must be a base64 / URI-list subscription (the v2rayN kind); Clash YAML is not parsed. Re-synced hourly.
external.linksHint: One vless:// vmess:// trojan:// ss:// hysteria2:// tuic:// anytls:// link per line, or a whole base64 subscription body.
external.deleteSourceHint: Nodes synced from this subscription are removed with it.
external.hideDeadHint: The panel TCP-probes every node address every 10 minutes; nodes whose last probe failed are left out of subscriptions.

routing.title: Server routing
routing.hint: This configuration applies to the selected server’s proxy inbounds. Add outbounds, then select a default or use inbound:tag rules for specific inbounds. An outbound can connect through another outbound. Managed reverse connections keep their dedicated route.
routing.addFromLink: Add an outbound from a share link
routing.rawHint: Passed to the core untranslated in its own dialect; normally not needed.
routing.defaultHint: Proxy traffic that matches no rule uses this exit. This does not change the server’s operating-system default route.
routing.matchHint: Comma separated: inbound:tag, domain:example.com, full:host, ip:1.2.3.0/24, geosite:netflix, geoip:cn, protocol:bittorrent, port:443
routing.balancerHint: Picks the member with the best URL test; rules and the default may point at it
routing.dnsHint: Resolvers the cores use for outbound names: 1.1.1.1, tls://…, https://…; blank = system DNS

subAdjust.title: Subscription adjustments
subAdjust.hint: Applies to the current subscription; the quota override and reset day survive renewals of the same plan and clear on a plan change.

speedtest.title: Speed test
speedtest.subtitle: Left: TCP connect latency from the panel to each subscription node's public address (what clients connect to). Below: latency and download throughput the servers measure themselves.
speedtest.nodeSideHint: Carrier latency and probe tasks. For download throughput add a task of type download in Settings → Probe with a large file URL (e.g. https://speed.cloudflare.com/__down?bytes=100000000); servers run it every 10 minutes and it uses real traffic.
speedtest.probeOff: The probe is off, so there is no server-side data.

tokens.title: API tokens & MCP
tokens.hint: Personal tokens for scripts and AI agents; they carry your role and are shown once. Call the admin API with an Authorization: Bearer header.
tokens.name: Name
tokens.showOnce: Copy it now; it will not be shown again:
tokens.mcpHint: Built-in MCP server at {{url}}. Point Claude Code, Cursor or any MCP client at it to query servers, users, orders, tickets and the probe in natural language; write tools require confirm=true.
tokens.permissionsHint: Choose resource:read / resource:write, or enter an exact API route such as GET /api/admin/users/{id}. Employee role and read-only limits still apply.

twofa.title: Two-factor authentication
twofa.hint: Add TOTP (Google Authenticator, 1Password, …) to this console account. Sign-in then needs a 6-digit code; API tokens are unaffected.
twofa.manual: or enter the key by hand:

tempLinks.title: Temporary subscription links
tempLinks.hint: Use- and/or time-limited subscription URLs to hand out for trials without exposing the permanent link; they expire on their own and can be revoked.

forwards.title: Port forwards (relay tunnels)
forwards.hint: Listen on this server and relay raw TCP/UDP to a landing server: clients connect here while auth and accounting stay on the landing inbound. Pick another server's inbound as the target and create a subscription node through this relay with one click. Ports must not collide with this server's inbounds.
forwards.pickInbound: Pick a server inbound, or type one
forwards.makeEntry: Create a subscription node through this relay
forwards.entryMade: Node created; rename it on the Nodes page
forwards.nftHint: Kernel DNAT supports same-family IPv4/IPv6 (bosun ≥ 0.62 for IPv6) and requires nft. Preserving the source requires the target to route replies through this server. Use relay/realm for cross-family forwarding.
forwards.backendRealmHint: bosun installs and runs a zhboner/realm relay: high throughput, hostname targets and UDP; no connection or traffic counters.
forwards.moreTargetsHint: Further next hops for the same rule: a backup line, or more lines to spread connections over. Health is a TCP connect every 30 s.
forwards.balanceFailoverHint: New connections go to the first target that passes its health check; a failed connect moves on to the next before the client notices.
forwards.balanceRoundRobinHint: New connections are spread over the healthy targets in proportion to their weights. One connection still uses one target.
forwards.realmRoundRobinOnly: realm spreads connections but cannot retry another target, so it only offers round-robin.
forwards.udpUntested: UDP health is not measured by a TCP connect or an open UDP socket.
forwards.tcpProbe: TCP connection test only; not an end-to-end proxy check.

backup.title: Database backups
backup.hint: A SQLite snapshot lands in {{dir}} once a day at the chosen hour; the newest N stay locally and each one can be pushed to WebDAV or an S3-compatible bucket (Cloudflare R2, Backblaze B2, MinIO). Restore: stop Captain, replace captain.db with a snapshot, start it again.
backup.pathStyleHint: For MinIO or hosts without bucket subdomains
backup.encryptHint: Sealed with age before upload; the bucket only ever holds ciphertext. Local copies stay plain, like the live database beside them.
backup.encryptOffWarn: Remote copies are uploaded unencrypted: they contain password hashes, payment keys and every subscription token.
backup.passphraseHint: At least 12 characters. Stored on the panel, so it protects the bucket, not this host. Keep a copy elsewhere.
backup.keyWarn: This is the only copy. Captain keeps the public key and cannot open its own remote backups; without this key nobody can. Store it outside this server, then save the settings.
backup.restoreHint: Restore a remote copy: captain backup open -identity key.txt -o captain.db FILE, or age -d -i key.txt FILE | gunzip > captain.db. An encrypted copy also carries config.yaml (base URL, payment keys — they are not in the database) and writes it beside the database.

certs.issueHint: Issued by Let’s Encrypt through Cloudflare DNS-01, usually within a minute; renewed 30 days before expiry. You can list example.com and *.example.com together.
certs.name: Name
certs.domainsHint: Enter or comma separated; wildcards as *.example.com
certs.dnsAuthHint: Blank = matched from the first domain against the registered ones.
certs.autoRenewHint: Re-issued by the panel 30 days before expiry.
certs.deleteHint: Servers using it fall back to automatic or local certificates.
certs.noIssuer: This panel has no data directory and cannot issue; uploads and the webhook still work.
certs.primaryHint: Blank = the first name in the certificate
certs.webhookHint: Certimate, acme.sh etc. POST JSON here after renewal: domain / domains, certificate, privateKey (private_key, key also accepted). Below is a Certimate body template.

domains.title: Domains & certificates
domains.subtitle: Register the domains you own, issue or upload certificates here; whichever server uses a name gets the matching certificate automatically.
domains.domainHint: A registrable domain such as example.com; server, subscription and panel host names live under it.
domains.tokenHint: Only when this domain lives in another Cloudflare account; blank uses the global token from Settings → ACME.
domains.tokenGlobalHint: Blank uses the global token from Settings; set one only for a domain in another account.
domains.tokenSet: Saved; blank keeps it, "-" clears it.
domains.deleteHint: Removes the registration only; servers and certificates stay.
domains.autoDNSHint: When a server domain or line entry domain falls under this domain, saving the server or ingress creates/updates the A/AAAA record on Cloudflare (server public address / entry IP). The token needs DNS edit permission.

ingress.title: Ingresses and port mappings
ingress.hint: Record NAT or dedicated-line public entries, local addresses and available ports. Inbounds and forwards share the restrictions; subscriptions use mapped public addresses. Direct public servers need no ingress.
ingress.name: Name
ingress.bindIPHint: Local interface address inherited by inbounds and forwards; blank listens on all addresses.
ingress.lineIPHint: Far-end line address a relay connects to; optional for NAT.
ingress.entryHostHint: Public IP or hostname clients actually dial; required for NAT.
ingress.portOffsetHint: entry port = local port + offset, usually 0
ingress.noEntryHint: This line has no public entry: add a port forward on a relay server that can reach it (target = the far-end address) and use the relay's address in subscription nodes.
ingress.deleteHint: An ingress still used by an inbound or forward cannot be deleted. Reassign or remove those configurations first.
ingress.entryDomainHint: A name for the public entry: subscription nodes advertise it instead of the IP; with auto DNS on the registered domain, an A record pointing at the entry IP is created automatically.
ingress.reservedHint: Provider-owned local ports, such as SSH, separated by commas. Neither inbounds nor forwards may use them.
ingress.deriveHint: nobrand's derived-tail policy: for a local address ending in N, reserve N×100 and use N×100+1 to N×100+99 as the pool.
ingress.mappingsHint: Enter a local range and its first public port per row. Use equal start/end values for a single port. Ranges cannot overlap; mappings apply to TCP and UDP.
ingress.requireIngress: Require an ingress on this server
ingress.requireIngressHint: Every inbound and forward must select an ingress. Existing configurations are checked before saving. Leave off if other interfaces need direct listeners.
ingress.providerHint: This records existing provider mappings; it does not configure their NAT or firewall. After changing mappings, review existing subscription node addresses.

warp.title: Cloudflare WARP exit
warp.hint: Register a WARP account on the server and send traffic through a WireGuard tunnel so it exits from Cloudflare's addresses. Use it when the VPS IP is refused by ChatGPT, Netflix and the like, with rules below so only those sites take it. Keys stay on the server.
warp.licenseHint: The 26-character key from the 1.1.1.1 app switches the account to WARP+
warp.templateHint: Route AI and streaming sites through WARP:

security.title: Console access control
security.hint: Restrict where the admin console and its API may be used from. API tokens are limited too.
security.allowCidrsHint: IPs or CIDRs; blank = anyone. A list that would lock you out is refused

overrides.title: Config overrides
overrides.hint: A JSON object per core, deep-merged into the rendered config: objects merge field by field, arrays and scalars replace, null deletes a field. For core options the panel does not expose. A bad override stops the core; the doctor shows it.

userEntries.title: Subscription nodes
userEntries.hint: Nodes available to this user. Each share link contains the user’s own credentials. Turning a node off hides it only from this user’s subscription.
userEntries.noLink: No share link for this protocol

subDesign.title: Visual designer
subDesign.hint: Choose a preset, add optional enhancements, then preview and apply the selected client formats. Loading or syncing a preset does not change published subscriptions.
subDesign.presetConfirm: Loading a preset replaces the groups and rules being edited (unapplied changes are lost).
subDesign.groupsHint: Members can be all servers, a tag, a region, or another group. select is manual, url-test chooses by measured latency, fallback uses the first available server, and load-balance distributes traffic.
subDesign.noGroups: No groups yet; load a preset to start.
subDesign.rulesHint: Matched top to bottom, first hit wins. Keep GEOIP CN after the China domain/IP lists; the final policy takes everything else.
subDesign.saveHint: Saving a draft does not update published subscriptions. Generate and apply again to publish changes.
subDesign.applyConfirm: Generate and replace the global templates for: {{formats}}. Other formats remain unchanged.
subDesign.applyHint: Generated templates can still be hand-edited under "Text"; the next "Generate & apply" overwrites those edits. Placeholders:
subDesign.applyScopeHint: Profile templates and response-rule templates still take priority. This does not override them.
subDesign.basicPreset: Basic: China direct, everything else through proxies
subDesign.syncHint: Sync updates the library only. Your draft, custom presets and published templates are retained.
subDesign.synced: Preset library synced; published templates unchanged
subDesign.notSynced: Official presets have not been synced yet.
subDesign.saveAsHint: Save a copy of this design and its enhancement choices. This does not apply it or change your draft.
subDesign.deletePresetConfirm: Delete “{{name}}” from the library? The current draft and published templates remain unchanged.
subDesign.presetDeleted: Preset removed; draft and published templates retained
subDesign.officialNotesEmpty: No introductory notes were found in the official file. View the source file for details.
subDesign.officialNotesHint: Original introductory comments from the synced preset. They may not describe every difference; also review the configuration preview.
subDesign.officialNotesDifferentRevision: These notes describe the updated preset library. Your draft still uses the version originally loaded.
subDesign.officialNotesSource: View this version of the official source file
subDesign.enhancementsHint: Options are saved separately from the base. Preview shows the combined output and each format’s support.
subDesign.regionsHint: Add missing region selectors with an automatic option and every server in that region. Empty generated region groups are hidden unless a rule or default policy explicitly uses them; then they remain and reject connections. Existing custom groups are preserved.
subDesign.dnsHint: Generate proxied encrypted DNS and separate resolver settings for direct traffic and proxy-server names. Does not force TUN on.
subDesign.autoDNSPolicy: Automatic: follow Claude or create a DNS group
subDesign.claudeHint: Route requests to Claude service domains through the selected proxy group. For a stable exit, select a fixed node in that group.
subDesign.autoClaudePolicy: Create a Claude group with manual node selection
subDesign.webrtcHint: Block common STUN/TURN discovery paths. May affect calls and does not cover all WebRTC traffic.
subDesign.protectionLimit: These options generate client configuration, not a verified leak-test result. System/browser settings and whether traffic enters the proxy still matter.
subDesign.quicHint: Block UDP port 443, commonly used by HTTP/3. This is separate from WebRTC protection and may affect some services.
subDesign.unchangedFormats: This version has not yet adapted the selected rules or enhancements for these formats; their existing templates will be retained: {{formats}}.
subDesign.effectiveCount: Combined result: {{groups}} groups · {{rules}} rules (generated additions are included in the preview).
subDesign.previewHint: Template preview includes enhancements. Actual nodes are filled in for each user according to their permissions; this is not a connectivity test.
subDesign.supportImported: This version has not yet adapted the selected imported or inline rules for these formats.
subDesign.supportDNS: This version has not yet adapted DNS protection for these formats.
subDesign.supportClaude: This version has not yet adapted Claude rule priority for these formats.
subDesign.supportWebRTC: This version has not yet adapted WebRTC mitigation for these formats.
subDesign.supportQUIC: This version has not yet adapted the UDP 443 restriction for these formats.
subDesign.supportTimeout: This version has not yet adapted the imported health-check timeout for these formats.
subDesign.claudeRulesSyncHint: Update the library, review its changes, then adopt a version into your draft. Preview and apply the draft to update subscriptions.
subDesign.claudeRulesSyncFailed: Update failed. The previous library and published subscriptions are retained.
subDesign.claudeRulesNotSynced: Using built-in rules; not synced yet
subDesign.claudeRulesDraftPinned: Retains its selected version until you adopt another
subDesign.claudeRulesAppliedUnknown: Version unknown: no matching record for the current template
subDesign.claudeRulesAppliedHint: Each format shows its own global template version. Applying selected formats leaves the others unchanged. Subscription profiles or response rules may override these templates; clients must refresh their subscription.
subDesign.claudeRulesNoChanges: No domain rule changes in this comparison.
subDesign.claudeRulesSyncedHint: These changes compare the previous library with the updated version. Your draft and published subscriptions have not changed.
subDesign.claudeRulesAdoptHint: These changes compare your current draft with this library version. Adopting it only changes the draft; preview and apply to update subscriptions.
subDesign.claudeRulesDraftChanged: The draft has changed since this review opened. Close this dialog and review again before adopting.
subDesign.supportDNSDirectOnly: Surfboard sends encrypted DNS directly and cannot apply the selected DNS proxy policy.
subDesign.warningDNSStashVersion: DNS protection requires Stash iOS/tvOS 3.6+ or macOS 4.3+ for independent proxy hostname resolution.
subDesign.warningDNSSurgeIPProxies: Surge DNS protection requires all subscription proxy endpoints to use IP addresses. The subscription is rejected if it contains hostname endpoints, to prevent DNS from falling back to a direct connection.
subDesign.warningDNSDomesticSuffix: Only .cn domains use the direct domestic resolver. Other domestic domains use the selected proxied DNS resolver.
subDesign.warningDNSEgernProxyDirect: Egern’s default DNS uses the selected proxy policy. Its separate proxy DNS path remains encrypted and direct, bypassing per-domain Forward assignments.
subDesign.supportInlineRule: This inline rule cannot be represented in the selected format: {{detail}}
subDesign.supportUDPRuleOrder: Quantumult X can reject UDP destination ports only as a leading tunnel filter. Rules later in the list or using a different policy cannot be preserved.
subDesign.supportGroupTimeout: This client cannot preserve the group’s health-check timeout: {{detail}}
subDesign.supportGroupTestURL: This client cannot preserve different test URLs across groups: {{detail}}
subDesign.supportHTTPTestURL: Surfboard supports only HTTP health-check URLs.
subDesign.warningNativeRulePriority: Loon applies its native rule priority: domain matches before IP matches, and local rules before remote rules.
subDesign.warningLoonRuleVersion: UDP port restrictions require Loon 3.1.7 or later.
subDesign.warningQXUDPTunnel: Quantumult X UDP port restrictions apply only to traffic captured by its tunnel.
subDesign.supportDNSLoonPolicy: Loon’s documented profile settings cannot guarantee the selected DNS proxy policy. Disabling fallback from encrypted to plain DNS also requires an app setting.
subDesign.supportDNSQXPolicy: Quantumult X’s documented DNS settings cannot bind local encrypted DNS queries to the selected proxy policy. Proxied destinations use remote resolution.
subDesign.supportRemoteRules: This remote source contains rules the client cannot represent equivalently: {{detail}}
subDesign.warningRemoteProcessMacOS: This rule resource includes process rules that only work on macOS; iOS/tvOS ignore them.
subDesign.warningRemoteNativeUnsupported: The existing Mihomo rule resource is retained for compatibility, but it contains URL-REGEX, which Mihomo does not support; this resource is not fully equivalent.
subDesign.regionMembersHint: Region matching uses the subscription node’s registered region first, or its name when no region is set. Existing name-pattern conditions keep their original behavior.
subDesign.nodeDualStackHint: Enable IPv6 and concurrent dialing so supported nodes can use the first working IPv4/IPv6 connection. These are global Mihomo dialer options and may also affect direct connections.
subDesign.nodeDualStackRequirements: Use a node domain with A and AAAA records. If one address family fails, the other reachable path can still connect. Literal IPs and explicit single-stack overrides are preserved. Does not force TUN or application DNS AAAA responses.
subDesign.supportNodeDualStack: Dual-stack connection selection currently supports Mihomo only; published templates for other formats remain unchanged.
subDesign.nodeDualStackTCP: TCP dialing: VLESS, VMess, Trojan, Shadowsocks (including ShadowTLS), AnyTLS, Snell, SOCKS5 and HTTP(S). Applies to published nodes supported by the client.
subDesign.nodeDualStackQUIC: Hysteria2 and TUIC: current Mihomo versions race QUIC connections; exact behavior depends on the core version.
subDesign.nodeDualStackOther: Mieru and WireGuard can use IPv4 or IPv6, but this option does not guarantee connection racing. SSH and Naive are not supported by the current Mihomo subscription renderer.

hwid.title: Devices (HWID)
hwid.hint: Devices identified by the x-hwid header that Happ, FlClashX, V2Box, Streisand and similar clients send when fetching the subscription. Over the limit a device gets an empty subscription with the reason in headers.

responseRules.title: Response rules
responseRules.hint: Evaluated top to bottom on every subscription request; the first matching rule decides the format, extra headers and template, or refuses the request. No match: the format is guessed from the User-Agent as before.
responseRules.empty: No rules: every client gets the format guessed from its User-Agent.
responseRules.name: Name
responseRules.catchAll: No condition: this rule matches every request (put it last).
responseRules.headersHint: One per line, Name: value (e.g. profile-update-interval: 12).
responseRules.templateHint: Replaces the format's template for requests hitting this rule. Empty: the normal template.

connlog.title: Connection log
connlog.hint: Servers report every accepted connection: user, client address, destination host and port. Shown per user in the user drawer, for abuse reports and support. Needs bosun ≥ 0.42; mieru inbounds are not covered.
connlog.privacy: This is personal data about what your users visit. Keep it off unless you need it, keep the retention short, and say so in your privacy notice. Switching it off deletes what was collected.
connlog.none: No connections recorded (is the connection log on?)
connlog.maxPerUserHint: The newest rows one account keeps

audit.title: Audit rules
audit.hint: Rules every server enforces: "block" rejects the connection on sing-box, xray and hysteria and reports the hit; "log" only reports. Hits are kept 90 days. mieru inbounds cannot block or report.
audit.name: Name
audit.matchHint: Match syntax: domain:example.com (and subdomains), full:host, keyword:text, regexp:^bet[0-9]+\., ip:198.51.100.0/24, port:6881-6889, inbound:tag, protocol:bittorrent, geosite:category-ads-all, geoip:cn. Several entries of different kinds must all hold; entries of the same kind are alternatives.
audit.autoBanHint: 0 = never. Staff accounts are never banned.
audit.notify: Telegram admin chat on every hit

dynlimit.title: Dynamic speed limit
dynlimit.hint: A user whose average rate across all servers stays above the trigger for the trigger window is limited to the given speed for a while, then gets their plan limit back. Servers shape it like a plan limit (Linux with nft and tc). Applied from the next report; only ever tightens.
dynlimit.windowsHint: HH:MM-HH:MM in the panel's local time, may cross midnight; empty = always.
dynlimit.unlimited: Also throttle users with no speed limit
dynlimit.unlimitedHint: They have no shaper on the server yet, so applying and lifting a throttle reloads the cores serving them and drops their connections. Off: only users who already have a speed limit are throttled.

heartbeat.title: Panel heartbeat
heartbeat.hint: Captain fetches this URL on a schedule, so an external watchdog (healthchecks.io, Uptime Kuma push, Better Stack) alerts when the panel itself stops — crash, disk, network, anything. It works behind NAT and Cloudflare Tunnel because the panel calls out.

adminlog.title: Console activity
adminlog.hint: Every change made through the console or an API token: who, what route, and what it answered. Reads are not recorded. Kept 180 days; admins only.

msg.heartbeat_off: nothing watches the panel itself; point the heartbeat at an external monitor
msg.mail_off: no mail provider: password resets, verification codes and expiry reminders cannot be sent
msg.staff_2fa_missing: {{count}} staff account(s) sign in with a password only: {{emails}}
msg.dns_pending: {{count}} DNS checks are stale or unconfirmed

accountID.inUse: This ID is occupied or reserved by historical records.

siteReset.title: Reset site
siteReset.description: Clear Captain’s business data and console settings to start again.
siteReset.warning: Users, other staff accounts, plans, orders, subscriptions, servers, certificates stored in the panel, statistics and all console settings will be deleted. Back up anything you need before continuing.
siteReset.previewFailed: Could not load the reset preview.
siteReset.admin: Keep {{email}} as administrator ID 1, with the same password and enabled two-factor authentication. All sessions, API tokens, subscription links and server pairings will be revoked. Sign in again after resetting.
siteReset.preserved: Deployment files (config.yaml, HTTPS certificates and custom static site files), existing backups and external DNS records are kept. Configuration supplied in config.yaml, including payment gateways, still applies.
siteReset.nodesWarning: Remote bosun programs and their cached configurations are not removed. Servers may continue serving old users. Stop or clean up those servers before resetting, then pair them again.
siteReset.nodesAcknowledge: I have handled the remote servers and understand that resetting Captain will not stop them.
siteReset.codeHint: Enter a fresh code that has not already been used to sign in.
siteReset.confirmationHint: Type RESET exactly to confirm deletion.

nodeRemoval.title: Remove {{name}}
nodeRemoval.standalone: Keep bosun and switch to standalone
nodeRemoval.requires: Remote actions require an online server with bosun v0.55.0+, installed by the standard Linux systemd/OpenRC script. Containers must be managed on the host.
nodeRemoval.standaloneHint: Keeps the currently provisioned inbounds, users, access restrictions and forwards. Captain plans, billing records and subscription URLs are not transferred.
nodeRemoval.loginHint: Existing local administrator credentials are kept. A previously headless server listens on 127.0.0.1:2053; set its login password over SSH and restart bosun, then use an SSH tunnel or configure a reverse proxy.
nodeRemoval.uninstallHint: Stops bosun and its proxy cores, removes the service, executable and configuration, and deletes local data unless you choose to keep it.
nodeRemoval.keepData: Keep local data, cores and certificates
nodeRemoval.recordHint: Only the panel record and its inbounds are deleted. This does not switch bosun to standalone or uninstall it; running proxies may continue with old configuration.
nodeRemoval.waiting: Waiting for the server to finish. The Captain record is kept until the worker reports success.
nodeRemoval.finished: The server operation succeeded. Finish removing its Captain record.
nodeRemoval.incomplete: The server has not confirmed successful completion. Its record was kept.
nodeRemoval.timeout: Timed out waiting for the server. Its record was kept; reopen this dialog to check the task.
nodeRemoval.intro: The server and its inbound records will be removed from Captain. Choose what happens to bosun on the server.

resources.title: Host resources
resources.hint: Unavailable measurements are shown as —. Rates need two valid samples.
resources.legacy: Detailed resources require bosun v0.56.0 or later.
resources.networkHint: Only selected interfaces contribute to host totals. Interface counters start at interface creation or counter reset; they are separate from server cycle traffic and user proxy billing.
resources.processHint: CPU: 100% equals one logical CPU. RSS is resident memory; only bosun and its supervised processes are shown.
resources.selectionHint: Use exact interface names. An empty include list automatically filters loopback, Docker and bridge interfaces. From v0.76.1, bosun also excludes its managed WireGuard and traffic-shaping interfaces; older agents need an upgrade. Exclusions take precedence. Newly selected interfaces start counting from the next sample.

monitoring.title: Monitoring
monitoring.hint: Live resources and history across your servers.
monitoring.historyHint: Minute buckets: 24 hours; hourly: 14 days; daily: 90 days. Gaps mean no valid sample. Peaks are maxima within each bucket.
monitoring.noHistory: No valid samples in this range. Enable monitoring collection and wait for server reports.
monitoring.truncated: The metric limit was reached; some device series were omitted.
monitoring.groupHint: Independent from user groups. Empty removes this grouping; group names also appear on the status page.
monitoring.compareHint: Choose up to four servers to compare the same metric.
monitoring.publicHint: Hidden sections are also removed or masked in the public API. Device and process details always stay private.

networkQuality.title: Network quality
networkQuality.liveHint: Rolling values use the last 30 attempts. Missing phases are —; a measured zero remains zero.
networkQuality.semantics: TCP requires a successful connection. Carrier/line TCP reachability also accepts refusal. HTTP uses one GET, accepts 200–399, and does not follow redirects. Response wait excludes DNS, connect and TLS. Jitter is the mean absolute change between adjacent successes; failures break the pair.
networkQuality.historyHint: History counts unique attempts. P50/P95 are approximate (error ≤5% or 0.1 ms). Gaps and unsupported old-agent metrics stay empty. Phase averages include completed phases only.
networkQuality.noHistory: No measurements for this metric and period.
networkQuality.skipped: {{count}} attempts were not received; they are unknown, not target failures.

availability.title: Availability
availability.hint: Measures server contact with Captain, not proxy or end-to-end service uptime. Availability = online / observed time outside maintenance.
availability.observationHint: Unknown intervals are excluded from availability and reduce coverage. History starts with this upgrade; panel restarts and observation gaps over two minutes remain unknown.

alerts.title: Alert events
alerts.hint: One incident per ongoing condition. Acknowledge records who is handling it; it does not resolve or mute the incident. Open and recovery notifications use the existing Telegram/webhook channels.
alerts.windowHint: Both modes keep recording incidents. Maintenance suppresses notifications and excludes its time from availability; silence only suppresses notifications. A still-active incident can notify after its window ends. Canceling keeps elapsed maintenance history.
alerts.localTime: Uses your browser’s local time zone
alerts.durationHint: 1 minute to 30 days; past windows cannot be added
alerts.invalidDate: Enter a valid start time and duration
alerts.truncated: Showing up to 200 windows, with active and scheduled windows first

diagnostics.title: Network diagnostics
diagnostics.hint: Run a check from this server. One task at a time; up to 35 seconds.
diagnostics.downloadHint: Download only: up to 8 seconds or 64 MiB. This uses server traffic; the result is not total link capacity.
diagnostics.routeHint: Up to 20 hops; MTR sends 5 rounds. System mtr/traceroute is required. Missing replies alone do not prove packet loss at the destination.
diagnostics.serviceHint: DNS returns A/AAAA addresses. TCP requires a connection; HTTP checks the response without following redirects.
diagnostics.installHint: Install mtr or traceroute on the server to use this check, then retry.
diagnostics.requirement: Requires an online bosun v0.56.0 or newer. Full administrators only.

outcomes.install_failed: Diagnostic tool download or verification failed

probeAppearance.hint: Only affects the status page. Inherit uses the existing site settings; presets are bundled and load no external code.

directory.loadFailed: Could not load users. Check the filters and retry.

results.history: Financial or invitation history; keep banned
results.no_subscription: No active row for selected plan

metadata.title: Internal notes and fields

passkeys.title: Passkeys

passkeys.needCode: Enter your authenticator code, then choose passkey sign-in again.

subProfiles.name: Name
subProfiles.inUse: This item is still assigned or selected as default. Remove those references before deleting it.
